work.title: Flutter 3.41 → 3.47.
work.lead: A production enterprise app with live users needed a two-step SDK jump, Apple's UIScene lifecycle and a move from CocoaPods to Swift Package Manager — without pausing releases.

teaser.label: Enterprise · migration
teaser.title: Flutter 3.41 → 3.47 with zero regressions
teaser.summary: A two-step SDK jump, UIScene and Swift PM, with releases never paused.

problem: Several plugins had dropped support for the old toolchain, the iOS build relied on CocoaPods specs being retired, and the scene-based lifecycle had an App Store deadline.
The constraint: releases could not stop. Every step had to land on main behind a green build.

steps.title: Audit the tree
steps.body: Every package mapped against the target SDK; blockers flagged first.

steps.title: Upgrade in steps
steps.body: SDK bump, then plugins, each behind a green CI build.

steps.title: Move iOS to SPM
steps.body: Pods replaced with Swift packages; UIScene adopted.

steps.title: Release and watch
steps.body: Staged rollout with crash monitoring before full release.

result.title: Shipped on schedule. No rollback.
result.body: The app moved to the current toolchain and stayed releasable at every step.

work.title: Crash reporting,
work.lead: A product team's crash reports and engineering tasks lived in paid third-party tools. I built two internal platforms that replaced them.

teaser.label: Internal tooling
teaser.title: A crash reporting platform built in-house
teaser.summary: Offline-capable; replaced a paid SaaS for the mobile team.

work.problemTitle: Paying rent on your own crash data.
problem: Costs grew with usage, data sat outside the company, and neither tool fitted how the team worked.
The new tools had to run alongside the old ones until the team trusted them, with no gap in crash visibility.

steps.title: Map the workflow
steps.body: How the team actually triaged crashes and tracked release work.

steps.title: Crash pipeline
steps.body: Offline queue on device, sync, grouping, stack traces with release metadata.

steps.title: Task tracking
steps.body: A board shaped around the team's release cycle, not a generic one.

steps.title: Switch over
steps.body: Both vendors removed once the team worked in the new tools.

result.title: Two vendors gone. Data stays home.
result.body: Crash data and engineering tasks now stay inside the company, in tools the team owns and can change.

work.title: Flutter 2 → 3.
work.lead: A large, maps-heavy enterprise telecom app was pinned to Flutter 2. It was in daily use, so a broken release was not an option.

teaser.label: Telecom · maps
teaser.title: Flutter 2 → 3 for an enterprise telecom app
teaser.summary: Maps-heavy codebase migrated with no regressions.

work.problemTitle: Every month on the old version made it riskier.
problem: Dependencies were ageing out and new platform requirements were landing. The app served field users every day.

steps.title: Audit first
steps.body: Every dependency and platform channel checked for Flutter 3 before touching code.

steps.title: Small steps
steps.body: Migrated in reviewable steps through the existing release process, no big-bang branch.

steps.title: Fix by module
steps.body: Breaking API changes fixed module by module, with regression checks at each step.

result.title: Upgraded. Unblocked.
result.body: The app moved to Flutter 3 with zero regressions reaching production, and the team could use current packages and SDK targets again.
